visual_goal: Show that commercial and payment objects describe intent and outcome, every object that moves money drops a balance transaction, and balance transactions are what payouts group and what the ledger is built from.
prompt: A compact diagram filling the frame, in three horizontal tiers on the left and a soft orange panel on the right. Top tier: three blue cards joined by single arrows, left to right: 'Subscription', 'Invoice', 'PaymentIntent'; one arrow from 'PaymentIntent' down into the first card of the middle tier. Middle tier: four teal cards side by side, evenly spaced: 'Charge', 'Refund', 'Dispute', 'Transfer'. Bottom tier: a long shallow tray filled with small receipt slips, labeled 'Balance transactions', running under all four teal cards. Each of the four teal cards has exactly one straight dotted arrow pointing down into the tray, carrying one receipt slip, so there are four parallel dotted arrows. Right panel (light orange): from the tray one arrow up-right into a tied bundle of slips with a coin labeled 'Payout', and one arrow right into an open book labeled 'Ledger'. Exactly nine arrows.
alt: Subscription, Invoice, PaymentIntent and Charge in a chain; Charge leads to Refund, Dispute and Transfer; each money-moving object drops a slip into a tray of balance transactions, which feeds the payout bundle and the ledger book.

visual_goal: Show the same 180.00 routed two ways: under destination charges the gross amount, fee and dispute risk pass through Tablekin's balance; under direct charges only the 0.54 application fee does.
prompt: A diagram with two horizontal rows separated by a thin line. Upper row, labeled at its left edge 'Destination charge': a stack of coins labeled '180.00' flows through one thick green pipe into a large orange jar labeled 'Tablekin'. From the jar two pipes leave: a thick pipe right into a jar labeled 'Venue' and a thin pipe up into a plain box labeled 'Stripe'. A small amount of coins stays in the Tablekin jar, labeled '0.54'. Lower row, labeled at its left edge 'Direct charge': a stack of coins labeled '180.00' flows through one thick green pipe straight into a large jar labeled 'Venue'. From the Venue jar a thin pipe leaves into a plain box labeled 'Stripe', and a very thin pipe leaves into a small orange jar labeled 'Tablekin', carrying one coin labeled '0.54'. In the upper row the Tablekin jar is large and full; in the lower row it is small. Exactly six pipes.
alt: Two rows: under a destination charge the 180.00 flows into Tablekin's jar and out to the venue and Stripe, leaving 0.54; under a direct charge the 180.00 flows into the venue's jar and only the 0.54 fee reaches Tablekin.

visual_goal: Show the Tablekin invoice crossing three time boundaries, usage earned in March, invoiced and paid on 1 April, paid out on 5–6 April, each with its own journal.
prompt: A horizontal timeline ribbon from left to right divided into three segments by two vertical dashed lines. First segment labeled 'March': a usage meter dial with a small accrual note labeled '780'. Second segment labeled '1 Apr': an invoice document labeled '1,029' with a few coins beside it. Third segment labeled '5–6 Apr': a bank building with one arrow of coins entering it. Below each of the three segments, a small open book, each with its own short arrow from the segment above down into it; the three books together are captioned once 'separate journals'. One long arrow runs along the ribbon from left to right. Exactly four arrows.
alt: A timeline in three segments: usage metered in March with a 780 accrual, the 1,029 invoice paid on 1 April, and the payout reaching the bank on 5 to 6 April, each segment posting its own journal into a separate book.

visual_goal: Show that webhooks serve operations while the finance path runs from Data Pipeline through one normalized layer shared with Adyen to the brand ledgers and BlackLine, reaching consolidation only through the ledgers.
prompt: A left-to-right diagram. At the far left, a plain box labeled 'Stripe'. From it, one thin arrow with a lightning bolt runs up to a box at the top labeled 'Brand operations', set apart on a grey panel. From 'Stripe', one thick arrow labeled 'Data Pipeline' runs right into a wide funnel labeled 'Normalized layer'. Below 'Stripe', a plain box labeled 'Adyen' with one arrow up-right into the same funnel. From the funnel three arrows leave to the right: one into an open book labeled 'Workday', one into an open book labeled 'Oracle Fusion', and one down into a box with interlocking puzzle pieces labeled 'BlackLine'. A bank building labeled 'Bank' at the bottom with one arrow into 'BlackLine'. At the far right, a box labeled 'OneStream' at the height of the two books, receiving one arrow from 'Workday' and one arrow from 'Oracle Fusion'; 'BlackLine' sits lower down, near the bank, and is joined only to the funnel and the bank. Exactly nine arrows.
alt: Stripe webhooks go to brand operations; Stripe's Data Pipeline and Adyen feed one normalized layer, which feeds the Workday and Oracle Fusion ledgers and BlackLine, with the bank also feeding BlackLine and only the ledgers feeding OneStream.
